item.title: Version 2.0.21
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • The board header follows the new design: the controls capsule sits on its own row at the top right, with the greeting below it; the date, next meeting and current task read in semibold.
  • The subtask Play button uses Apple's filled play symbol.
  • To Do cards follow the new design: every task in a project group gets its own tile with its own move-to-Today arrow; the group's collapse chevron and the "move the whole group" row are gone (drag the group header to move it all). The column title reads "To do".

Fixed

item.title: Version 2.0.20
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • The Backlog column is now called To Do, everywhere it appears (board, menus, QuickTask and Sync Finder settings).
  • The main board follows the new design: roomier columns and cards without outlines, a running Today card tinted in the accent color, a cleaner card header, an outlined Subtasks panel with Details tiles, and subtask rows with a new Play/Stop button. The To Do hours, the Today task count and the Today progress bar are gone.
  • Every task inside a card now sits on its own tile (the running one in green), project group cards drop their dividers and show the group's total as "Estimate Time", columns get a thin black outline, and the Subtasks panel's Details tiles share the width evenly.

Fixed

item.title: Version 2.0.19
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • Pressing Play on another Mac now moves every Mac to the new task. When two Macs start timers before seeing each other's, the newest start wins everywhere: the older session ends where the newer one began, closed by the Mac that started it (or by any Mac after a day, if that Mac never comes back). If the newer task has no Toggl project, the older task's Toggl entry is stopped too.
  • A timer stopped in Toggl is published to the other Macs right away instead of on their next check.

Fixed

  • A Mac kept showing the task it had started after another Mac started a different one: each Mac showed "the first" open session it found, and the old task stayed marked as running, so its Play did nothing.
  • Play failed with "This task requires a valid stage selection before tracking" when only another open subtask had a workflow stage.
  • Play failed when the running session belonged to a task this Mac had not received yet.
  • A fresh, never-used library could keep itself over the other Mac's library instead of adopting it.

item.title: Version 2.0.18
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • While a timer runs, the Mac that started it checks Toggl once a minute even in the background (was every 5 minutes), so a timer stopped in Toggl pauses in ToDoPro within a minute and, through iCloud, on every Mac. Other Macs check when you switch to them, or every 5 minutes as a fallback. With no timer running, ToDoPro no longer calls Toggl in the background.

Fixed

  • After adopting the other Mac's library, the next save could fail ("UNIQUE constraint failed: sync_changes…") and ToDoPro then refused every save until it was restarted: edits and timer changes, including a stop detected in Toggl, were not saved.
  • Time sessions recorded a new device identity on every launch, so after a restart a Mac no longer recognized its own sessions.

item.title: Version 2.0.17
item.description:
Added

Changed

Fixed

  • iCloud sync could stop for good with "The synchronization envelope is invalid." on a Mac that fell behind: it received every pending change in one page, over the limit, and rejected it on every retry. Changes now arrive in batches of 32 and a Mac catches up in one pass.
  • A time session from the other Mac for a task, subtask or project this Mac had not received yet rejected the whole page, including the library that would bring them, so the two Macs showed different projects. Such sessions are now kept and the page applies.

item.title: Version 2.0.16
item.description:
Added

Removed

  • About 1,460 lines of unused code found by Periphery, including an unused iCloud "recent changes" pull and the backup validator of the removed JSON import.
  • The legacy JSON backup import, which no button in Settings opened anymore (the portable backup replaced it).

Changed

  • Edit times never go backwards, even if the Mac's clock does, and moving a task or note on the board now counts as an edit. Both prepare for syncing each task separately.
  • Opening a library saved by a newer ToDoPro now says to update the app (the data was already left untouched).
  • The board sorts each lane once per change instead of on every read (one render on a 2,000-task library: 0.26 s → 0.02 s).
  • Saving the library does less repeated work (one post-save verification instead of two, the database stays open, the rotating backup is only prepared when one is due): a save on a 2,000-task library takes about half as long.
  • The iCloud check every 5–15 seconds no longer decrypts and republishes the library when nothing changed, which redrew the whole board each time (50 idle checks on a 2,000-task library: 2.3 s → 0.04 s). It also pauses while ToDoPro is in the background with no timer running; switching back syncs right away.
  • Typing in a task editor no longer rewrites the whole library on every keystroke: edits made while a save is waiting join that save (40 keystrokes: 40 writes → 1).
  • Choosing a workflow stage that has no tag now keeps the task's or subtask's tags in every editor. The task editor and subtask sheet used to clear them while the inline subtask editor kept them.
  • Whether a timer is running, and which, now comes only from the local time ledger (shared across Macs through iCloud). The board, menu bar and launcher no longer show two running timers when a task's saved status and the ledger disagree.
  • Pending Toggl start and stop intents are now replayed on launch and during activity checks: a matching running entry is adopted, a closed local session is published as a finished entry, and an open session is restarted (bounded retries). An entry that another timer is running is never overwritten.
  • A timer stopped directly in Toggl now stops in ToDoPro within seconds of switching back to ToDoPro (or waking the Mac): those moments check Toggl at most every 20 seconds. Background checks stay at once every 5 minutes.
  • Board rows look up their project name in a table built once per change instead of scanning every project, and opening the board no longer re-reads the collapsed project groups on every redraw.
  • Choosing a portable backup, a time CSV or a task template no longer reads the file on the main thread, and a file over the size limit is refused before it is read (templates: 1 MiB).

Fixed

  • A library-deletion record arriving through iCloud, or a crafted portable backup tombstone, could erase every task, note and time session on this Mac. Nothing in ToDoPro sends one; such records are now ignored or rejected.
  • A task deleted on another Mac is now remembered as deleted here, and applying a task that came from another Mac no longer re-sends the whole library.
  • An edit made while Play, Pause or a subtask switch was being saved could be reverted, and a timer change could overwrite a library iCloud had just updated. Timer changes now commit against the exact library revision they read and re-apply only the timer fields.
  • Changing the work type of a subtask that was not being tracked did not save.
  • Edits saved right after Play, Pause or a subtask switch were silently discarded, including the Toggl running-entry id, so a later Pause or subtask completion could leave the Toggl timer running. Timer transactions now hand their saved revision to the next save.
  • An empty library synced from another Mac (for example a fresh install) could replace this Mac's tasks, projects and notes, either on arrival or through the automatic keep-newest pass. It now opens a sync conflict in Settings → Sync Issues instead.
  • Resolving an iCloud library conflict could restore an older or empty copy: "This Mac" now always means the library as it is now, and Keep Newest is unavailable when one side is empty.
  • An edit made just before an iCloud check could disappear and then be overwritten by the next edit. The check now waits for pending saves and never reloads over unsaved edits.
  • When a subtask switch was replayed after a lost Toggl response, the new start could be skipped and Toggl left with no running entry until a later check. The stop is now always replayed before the start.

Added

item.title: Version 2.0.12
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • Sync Now and timer presence now create the custom iCloud zone first, upload the latest library snapshot (not the historical backlog), then fetch zone changes. Background catch-up of the old default-zone journal waits until that live pass finishes and stops after the first successful zone fetch.
  • Library snapshots now converge automatically: the newer persisted copy wins (`syncedAt`, then latest task/note edit). A clock tie picks a stable device origin. Settings no longer asks for Keep Newest on every two-Mac session. Time overlaps still need a manual choice.

Fixed

  • The Mac that stayed on Connecting / Syncing was fetching the iCloud zone before uploading projects, and the other Mac never received library state because live `applicationState` pulls did not apply. Live zone changes now adopt the newer persisted library. An already-open library conflict is resolved on the next sync instead of waiting for a tap.
  • A save that lands one revision behind iCloud (for example Settings while CloudKit just wrote the library) reloads the disk snapshot and keeps the in-flight settings instead of showing “Todocky Could Not Load Your Data”.

item.title: Version 2.0.11
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • Sync Now shows “Connecting to iCloud…” immediately, pushes pending changes, and fetches the custom iCloud zone instead of replaying the historical journal. Catch-up of old default-zone records runs in the background, retries dropped connections, and is skipped once this Mac has already ingested remote changes.

Fixed

  • Settings no longer stays on Syncing / Connecting for minutes after Sync Now. The historical CloudKit journal no longer blocks timer presence or a connection check.

item.title: Version 2.0.10
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • Sparkle install now stops iCloud polling and idle work, flushes in the background, and always quits. A slow save no longer cancels Close, which left the installer waiting forever.

Fixed

item.title: Version 2.0.9
item.description:
Added

Changed

  • Timer presence now pushes the live interval immediately (interactive CloudKit QoS) and pulls only recent `timeSession` changes (about the last 3 minutes) instead of waiting for a full iCloud journal sync. Fallback poll is 1 second while a timer is visible and 2 seconds otherwise.

Fixed

item.title: Version 2.0.8
item.description:
Added

  • Running timer presence now syncs across Macs: Play on one machine shows Pause and live elapsed on the other within seconds, and starting a second task while one is already running is blocked.

Fixed

  • Elapsed time no longer stays at `00:00:00` after Play/Resume on a task with no previously closed time. The live session seconds are included even when there is no stored total yet.

item.title: Version 2.0.7
item.description:
Fixed

  • iCloud Sync Now retries a dropped CloudKit connection (`CKError.networkFailure` / `NSURLErrorNetworkConnectionLost`), uses user-initiated quality of service instead of a discretionary background transfer, pulls smaller journal pages, and shows a connection-interrupted message instead of `CKErrorDomain error 4`.
  • Invalid or zero Estimate Time (`0m`, empty, or unreadable input) now saves as no estimate instead of showing an Error alert.

item.title: Version 2.0.6
item.description:
Added

  • Added an explicit bulk resolver for CloudKit journal storms (`resolveOpenSyncConflicts`): one transactional decision per entity (Keep Newest / Keep All from This Mac / Keep All from Other Device), instead of one card per historical `applicationState` revision. Settings shows a storm summary when more than 20 rows are open or any entity has more than one open row.

Changed

  • Work Type is chosen when editing a subtask (briefcase icon next to billable/tags), not in the board view.
  • Settings → iCloud attention copy now reports library snapshots, journal rows, and time overlaps set aside, so a forked `applicationState` singleton is not described as hundreds of separate decisions.
  • Pull now compares canonical plaintext and keeps a single open conflict per entity. Historical revisions below local HEAD go to the inbox only, so CloudKit history cannot reopen a resolved storm.

Fixed

  • Play on a subtask and Resume now start time when the parent has no stage but an incomplete subtask does. Timer failures show the real local-database error, and an orphan open ledger session no longer leaves Resume dead when no task is running in the UI.
  • Live session now reloads the winning library after bulk conflict resolve so the next save isn’t a staleRevision miss.
  • Resolving one historical `applicationState` conflict no longer fails with UNIQUE `(entity_type, entity_id, entity_revision, operation)`: one-to-one resolve refuses when that entity has more than one open row, and bulk resolve emits a single successor at `max(known revisions)+1`.
  • Choosing a library snapshot during bulk resolve now materializes `applicationState` in the same transaction as the successor, so Keep Local cannot leave the library empty and Keep Remote actually becomes the local snapshot.
  • Settings no longer hangs while decrypting and painting every historical journal row during an `applicationState` storm.

item.title: Version 2.0.5
item.description:
Fixed

  • CloudKit sync now uploads large local backlogs in safe batches instead of exceeding the 400-record request limit. It also completes paged downloads, preserves unacknowledged changes after a failed batch, and prevents overlapping sync requests from duplicating work.
  • Settings → iCloud now uses a native switch and reports schema setup errors with the required CloudKit record type and container.

item.title: Version 2.0.4
item.description:
Added

  • Added TDPB v1 portable backups: a password-encrypted, authenticated, bounded backup format with preview-before-merge. Portable backups combine business records into the active library and exclude credentials, Keychain material, paths, sandbox bookmarks, Calendar state, and other device-local transport state.
  • Added the local CSV time-import foundation: bounded RFC-4180 parsing, explicit UUID mapping, Chicago/ISO-8601 timestamp validation, encrypted SQLite v8 import ledgers, HMAC deduplication, and a single transaction that commits closed imported sessions with their duration projection. The original 197-row fixture is still pending.
  • Added Increment 4 fail-closed database sync protocol scaffolding: encrypted v6 SQLite sync journal/outbox/inbox/cursor tables, an actor coordinator, and an unavailable-by-default transport that makes no CloudKit or network calls.
  • Added Settings → Sync Issues for the local sync journal. It clearly reports unavailable transport and lets a person resolve encrypted version conflicts or choose one of two overlapping time sessions; neither action enables CloudKit.
  • Added the first local-database increment: encrypted SQLite persistence with transactional revisions, deterministic local client/project identities, idempotent legacy-state migration, ordered app-state saves, and compatibility for existing backup APIs and legacy stage behavior.
  • Added the second local-database increment: an encrypted, durable local time-session ledger with exact start/stop timestamps, task/subtask/project/stage snapshots, work types, provenance, idempotent commands, and atomic task switches. Timer recording now commits locally before any Toggl request, so an offline or failed Toggl start never loses tracked time.
  • Added a durable encrypted Toggl time outbox that is committed in the same SQLite transaction as each local start, stop, or switch projection. After a lost Toggl response, relaunch reconciliation observes the remote entry and completes the queued intent without sending a duplicate request.
  • Subtask timer switches and checklist-driven subtask advances now commit the stop intent for the prior entry and the start intent for the new subtask alongside the ledger split and task snapshot. A relaunch can reconcile either side without losing or duplicating a remote transition.
  • Keyboard navigation for the board's inline subtask editor's Tags and Stage popovers: arrow keys move a highlight through the list, Return selects/toggles the highlighted item, and the search field is now focused automatically when either popover opens (previously you had to click into the filter field before arrow keys did anything). The list also auto-scrolls to keep the highlighted row in view as you navigate past the visible area.

Fixed

  • SyncFinderAgent no longer warns that `FavoritesSidebarService` is deprecated. That attribute was documenting Apple's deprecated-without-replacement `LSSharedFileList` API on the wrapper callers still have to use.
  • A tombstoned time session now removes any still-open overlap that references it in the same database transaction, so relaunch cannot present an unresolvable stale decision.
  • The tags picker (task editor, multi-task editor's subtasks, and the board's inline subtask editor) could show only a single tag the first time it was opened, requiring you to close and reopen it to see the full list. The Toggl tags fetch does complete correctly in the background, but SwiftUI's `.popover` wasn't reliably re-rendering its content once that fetch resolved while the popover was already open — it only picked up the fresh data on the next presentation. Fixed by keying each popover's content on the fetched tag count, forcing SwiftUI to redraw it as soon as the data lands.

ToDoPro 2

Encrypted local database, portable encrypted backups, resilient time tracking, and the foundation for secure sync.
